name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the state's failure to appoint counsel for an eligible defendant for an extended period violates the right to counsel under Article I, section 11 of the Oregon Constitution, and dismissal without prejudice is the required remedy after 60 or 90 days depending on the case type.

name: Flynn, C. J.
description: Other, did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the ballot title's caption, "yes" result statement, and summary needed modification to accurately reflect the measure's major effects, including the shift of discretion from school districts to parents and the non-speculative fiscal impact of funding following the student.

name: Ortega, P. J.
description: Concurred, argued that Measure 114 is a reasonable regulation to promote public safety and does not unduly frustrate the right to armed self-defense, thus being facially constitutional.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, authored the main opinion, finding that the defendant's mental health attributes did not provide a societal standard to reduce culpability for the crime committed with the requisite mental state, thus the mandatory minimum sentence was not disproportionate.

name: Balmer, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the majority's holding was more limited than the broad rule the defendant had proposed regarding personal characteristics in proportionality analysis.

name: Bushong, J.
description: Other, did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Duncan, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Court of Appeals erred in rejecting the defendant's appellate argument on preservation grounds, and remanded the case for further proceedings on the merits of the double jeopardy claim.

name: Bushong, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the majority opinion's detailed discussion of the merits of the double jeopardy claim and related legal principles was unnecessary dicta and should not influence the Court of Appeals on remand.

name: Baldwin, Senior Judge
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JAMES, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the lack of a "right" to employment does not, as a matter of law, prevent a plaintiff from proving economic damages for lost future wages, and that this is an issue of proof and causation, not pleading.

name: BUSHONG, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that a trial court's decision to deny a defendant's choice of retained counsel must be supported by an adequate record demonstrating a permissible exercise of discretion, which was lacking in this case.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Governor Kotek lacked the authority to revoke the plaintiff's conditional commutation because the plaintiff's sentence had already expired, and the terms of the commutation agreement did not grant such indefinite authority.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Governor's commutation rendered the petitioner's request for resentencing moot because he was no longer serving a death sentence, and that his challenges to penalty-phase questions were procedurally barred due to lack of preservation.

name: Walters, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
Masih, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JAMES, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Court of Appeals erred by analyzing the backpack seizure under a criminal framework instead of an administrative one, and that the seizure of the backpack was a significant interference with possessory interests.

name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the totality of circumstances, including the defendant's probation conditions, the location of the interrogation, and the pressure exerted, created a compelling environment requiring Miranda warnings.

name: Balmer, J.
description: Other, did not participate in the decision.

name: Walters, J.
description: Other, did not participate in the decision.

name: Nelson, J.
description: Other, did not participate in the decision.

name: BALMER, S. J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the state's conduct, including offering benefits and implicitly guiding Layman's investigation after the second proffer meeting, objectively conveyed that Layman was authorized to act as a state agent, thus violating the defendant's right to counsel.

name: Nelson, J.
description: Did not participate in the decision of this case.

name: James, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the UTPA provisions ORS 646.608(1)(b) and (1)(e) do not implicitly require proof that misrepresentations were "material to consumer purchasing decisions" and are not facially unconstitutional under free speech provisions.

Walters, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore

description: Did not participate in the decision of this case.

description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: James, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that detectives violated defendant's right to counsel under Article I, section 11, by questioning him about charged FIP crimes without counsel present, requiring suppression of the evidence.

name: NELSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that ORS 138.105(5) precludes appellate review of legal challenges to a conviction based on a guilty or no contest plea, as 'conviction' refers to the judicial determination of guilt reflected in the judgment entered in the trial court, and rejected constitutional challenges to this interpretation.

name: NELSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while the Court of Appeals erred in its reasoning regarding the materiality of the lost video and the defendant's guilty plea attempt, the defendant ultimately failed to establish a causal connection between the unexplained delay and the prejudice from the lost video, as the video would likely have been overwritten regardless of the delay.

name: BALMER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the five-day warrantless retention of the defendant's phone was unlawful, but the error in admitting derivative evidence was harmless, thus affirming the conviction.

name: Baldwin, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
DeHoog, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Oregon Constitution's Article I, section 11, grants a defendant the right to have counsel present in the grand jury room for consultation during testimony, but not for direct examination or formal evidentiary objections.

name: Garrett
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: DeHoog
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: BALMER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that voters with inactive registrations are not "qualified voters" under Article IV, section 1, because they are not presently eligible to vote, and therefore their signatures on initiative petitions cannot be counted.

name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion, which overruled the Brown per se exigency rule and affirmed the suppression of evidence because the state failed to prove actual exigent circumstances.

name: Landau, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
Balmer, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: KISTLER, S.J.
description: Concurred, argued that a defective waiver of a preliminary hearing does not deprive a circuit court of subject matter jurisdiction, reversing the Court of Appeals decision.

name: WALTERS, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the court has the authority to modify constitutional deadlines to ensure reapportionment occurs based on accurate federal census data, which is paramount to the voters' intent for fair representation, especially when original deadlines are impossible to meet due to unforeseen circumstances.

name: WALTERS, C.J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion, arguing that the trial court's order compelling the defendant to unlock her cell phone violated her right against self-incrimination because the state failed to meet the required burden of proof and did not prohibit the use of the compelled act against the defendant.
